title: Delhi Under Red Alert as Monsoon Deluge Triggers Flooding and Work-From-Home Orders
excerpt: IMD extends severe weather warning for Delhi-NCR as heavy rainfall causes waterlogging across key routes, prompting Gurugram authorities to advise offices to allow remote work.
body:
• IMD has issued a red alert for Delhi, warning of extremely heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and gusty winds across NCR
  • Gurugram police advised corporate offices to allow employees to work from home as waterlogging choked the Delhi-Gurugram Expressway
  • Delhi's IGI Airport issued a travel advisory urging passengers to check flight status before heading to the terminal
  • India's weather department forecasts below-average monsoon rainfall for August overall as El Niño conditions strengthen

Delhi and the National Capital Region were battered by intense monsoon showers on Wednesday as the India Meteorological Department extended a red alert for the capital, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and winds gusting up to 60 km/h. The downpour disrupted normal life across Delhi, Noida, Gurugram, Ghaziabad, and Faridabad, leaving roads flooded and commuters stranded during peak hours.

Roads Submerged, Commutes Doubled

Water accumulated rapidly on arterial roads and underpasses, turning the morning commute into a crawl. The Delhi-Gurugram Expressway — a critical artery for hundreds of thousands of office workers — was hit particularly hard, with vehicles backed up for kilometres in both directions. A section of NH-48 near Narsinghpur developed damage after continuous rainfall, forcing authorities to close two lanes and issue a traffic advisory.

Gurugram police took the unusual step of appealing to corporate offices to let employees work from home, aiming to reduce congestion on flooded roads. Several private companies adopted flexible arrangements for the day.

"The harm caused by this type of weather is compounded when key infrastructure fails. We urge residents to avoid unnecessary travel during intense spells."

— IMD Advisory Statement

Rainfall Hits Triple Digits in Ghaziabad

Overnight rainfall readings underscored the intensity of the current monsoon spell. Ghaziabad's Kamla Nehru Nagar station recorded 143 mm, while parts of south Delhi — Mehrauli at 83 mm, Lodi Road at 79 mm, and Pusa at 73 mm — also saw significant accumulations. Chhatarpur, Mayur Vihar, Janakpuri, and Narayana recorded between 57 mm and 68 mm. Gurugram and surrounding satellite cities saw comparable totals across multiple monitoring stations.

Airport Advisory Issued

Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport issued a passenger advisory asking travellers to check with their airlines before leaving for the terminal. Airport authorities said flight operations remained normal but warned that congested roads could significantly extend travel time to the airport. Ground teams were coordinating closely with airlines to minimise disruptions.

Civic Agencies Deploy Emergency Teams

Municipal authorities and emergency response teams were deployed at waterlogging hotspots across the capital. Pumps were activated at flood-prone underpasses, while traffic police were stationed at key intersections to prevent gridlocks. Authorities urged residents to stay away from waterlogged areas, avoid sheltering under trees during thunderstorms, and keep emergency supplies accessible.

Monsoon Outlook: Below Average for August

The severe weather in Delhi is part of a broader monsoon system affecting northern India, but the season's overall trajectory raises concerns. The IMD forecasts below-average monsoon rainfall for August, at less than 94% of the long-period average, as moderate El Niño conditions prevail and are expected to strengthen through September, according to Reuters.

India received 1% more rainfall than the long-period average in July, helping narrow the cumulative deficit from 35.4% at the end of June to 12.6%. But agricultural analysts warn that a weak August could affect crop growth at a critical juncture, particularly for rice and pulses planted during the kharif season.

What to Watch

IMD forecasts intermittent heavy showers to persist over Delhi-NCR through the coming days, with neighbouring states — Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh, and parts of Rajasthan — also under alert. Residents have been advised to monitor official weather updates and avoid non-essential travel during intense spells. For NRIs with family in the region, this is worth a check-in call — Delhi's annual monsoon disruptions can escalate rapidly from inconvenience to genuine safety risk.
nri_angle: NRIs with family in Delhi-NCR should check on relatives as city faces severe flooding, flight disruptions, and infrastructure strain during active monsoon spell.
